correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact p/q hypotheses, Kalton-property selection condition, detector min-bound and complete three-region index split. The 1st and 3rd tails sum with ratios s^{-2(q-p)} and s^{-2p}; at most one intermediate index exists. If there is one, neighboring tails gain s^{-(q-p)} and s^{-p}; if none, adjacent boundary scales force (h/b_r)(a_{r+1}/h)<=s^{-1}, hence at least one square-root gain. All missing-tail cases are smaller. Thus Lip(Phi)^p<=C G_s with G_s->1 for each fixed 0<p<q<=1. Given c<delta/(2^{1/p}Gamma_p), choose s with c Gamma_p G_s^{1/p}<delta/2^{1/p}, and then the strict finite-error tolerances from the cited selection proof; the normalization and strong Schur definition match the 2025 primary Definition 2.5. Unit vectors give upper coefficient norm <=1 by the p-triangle inequality. The endpoint q=p is excluded.
